description.narrative:
Barn i Sudan är i stor utsträckning fattiga i flera dimensioner och deras rättigheter är starkt kringskurna. Övergripande mål för insatsen är att möjliggöra att de mest utsatta barnen och ungdomarna i Sudan i ökad utsträckning får sina förutsättningar och rättigheter tillgodosedda och kan utvecklas i sin fulla potential i en inkluderande och skyddande miljö.
Insatsen består av fem komponenter; barns överlevnad och utveckling, utbildning och lärande, skyddande av barn, ett övergripande policy/evidensperspektiv som inkluderar ett socialförsäkringsmoment samt programeffektivitet. Ansats och interventionslogik bygger över lag på att stärka kapacitet och implementering på nationell och lokal nivå vad gäller tillgång(på tex service, stöd, skydd), efterfrågan(gm kunskap och resiliens) och gynnsam miljö(gm tex påverkansarbete vg lagar och policyer).
Insatsen är framtagen i samarbete mellan Sudans regering och UNICEF, i enlighet med Sudans Nationella Utvecklingsplan 2017-2020 och UNICEFs strategiska plan 2018-2021. Insatsens innehåll överensstämmer i stor utsträckning med Sveriges strategi för utvecklingssamarbete med Sudan 2018-2022 varför Sida föreslår ett stöd till landprogrammet fram till och med 2021. Insatsens totala budget är USD 241 050 000 och svenskt stöd utgör ca 6,5 procent.
UNICEF finansieras uteslutande av frivilliga bidrag från regeringar och privata givare. UNICEF Sudan får medel från UNICEF centralt och av ett antal regeringar direkt till sin landverksamhet. Insatserna genomförs i nära samverkan med aktörer, både statliga, NGOer och privata, på nationell och lokal nivå. 2017 samarbetade UNICEF med 63 genomförande partners. Ca 50 procent av medlen vidareförmedlas till genomförande partners.
Sida och UNICEF är avtalsparter genom en fastställd avtalsmall enligt beslut 2018/000956 för tematiskt stöd på landnivå. Avtalstiden löper till och med den 30 juni 2023 så att all finansiell rapportering ska komma in för de tematiska poolerna. UNICEF administrerar Sidas bidrag och implementerar programmet i enlighet med relevanta beslut från UNICEFs exekutiva styrelse och UNICEFS, regelverk, policyer och procedurer.
UNICEF kan ingå i avtal med implementerande parter och vidareförmedla medel utan att avtalskrav från avtalet tillhörande detta beslut inkluderas. Sida gör bedömningen att UNICEF har kapacitet att följa upp denna vidareförmedling. UNICEF ansvarar full ut för planering, implementering och uppföljning av insatsen i sin helhet.
I april 2018 var controllers från Sida Stockholm i Sudan för att göra bedömning av samarbetspartners kapacitet vad gäller interna processer, styrning och kontroll. UNICEF bedömdes ha adekvata rutiner för rapportering, budget, revision, vidarebefordring av medel samt kapacitet att i sin tur bedöma partners kapacitet.

The overall goal of the country programme is to "enable all children and adolescents in Sudan, especially those in the most vulnerable situations, to have their rights progressively fulfilled and to develop to their full potential in an inclusive and protective environment".
The UNICEF Country Programme in Sudan consists of five components: Child Survival and Development, Education and Learning, Child Protection, Policy, Evidence and Social Protection and Programme Effectiveness.
The contribution is created in cooperation between the Sudanese government and UNICEF, in line with the Government of Sudan's National Development Plan 2017-2020, and the UNICEF Strategic Plan 2018-2021.
The total budget for the Programme is USD 241 050 000, for 2018-2021. Suggested Swedish support to the contribution is 139 000 000 SEK over period 2019-2021.

The overall goal of the country programme of cooperation for 2018-2021 is to contribute to national efforts to enable all children and adolescents in Sudan, especially those in the most vulnerable situations, to have their rights progressively fulfilled and to develop to their full potential in an inclusive and protective environment. Expected outcomes: Health and Nutrition: By 2021, more children under the age of 5 years and women of reproductive age utilize high impact, quality health and nutrition services. WASH: By 2021, more children and their families are living in an open-defecation-free environment, using improved drinking water sources and adopting imporvied hygiene practices. Education and Learning: By 2021, more children have access to early stimulation and quality basic education and learning in inclusive and safe school environments. Child Protection: By 2021, more girls and boys are protected from violence , abuse and exploitation and benefit from improved response and prevention systems. Policy Evidence and Social Protection: By 2021, disadvanteged and excluded children are benefiting from an improved policy environment and strengthened social protection system. Programme Effectiveness: The country programme is efficiently designed, coordinated, managed and supported to meet quality programming standards.

During Covid UNICEF prepared and procured critical stock to ensure the availability of essential supplies during the pandemic. UNICEF Sudan took leadership roles in the three of the eight national response pillars of infection prevention and control (IPC), risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), and case management (as co-lead). Among the results are that a total of 488,157 people in COVID-19 high risk sites were reached with infection prevention and control supplies, hygiene promotion and sanitation as well as water supply facilities; the Health Promotion Unit of the Ministry of Health, in coordination of UNICEF and the World Health Organisation (WHO), completed the review and update of the 'Safe Return Protocol', which provided practical guidelines on the opening of schools; 20 million people were reached with awareness raising the messages on COVID-19 via SMS; UNICEF on behalf of the Global COVAX Facility led procurement and distribution of vaccines. In March, 2021, when the AstraZeneca vaccine arrived at Khartoum International Airport, Sudan became the first country in the MENA region to receive COVID-19 vaccines through the COVAX Facility. UNICEF has successfully used Justice for Children as a key entry point and platform for strengthening CP systems in Sudan. With greater coordination between the police, judiciary, prosecutors and CP case management systems, there have been significant improvements in linking the justice and law enforcement sectors as part of a broader CP system. This is especially true during the transition period. When it became possible to work with normative issues after the revolution in 2019, UNICEF was quick to take advantage of the new opportunities. This has also been possible because they have been in Sudan for a long time and have a large formal and informal network. In comparison to 2021, UNICEFs programmes in 2022 alone contributed to a two percent increase in the proportion of the population using an improved source of drinking water (from 76 per cent to 78 per cent), and one percent increase for population using an improved sanitation facility (from 37 per cent to 38 percent). UNICEF is leading the WASH Sector humanitarian coordination at national and at state level in 14 states, effectively coordinating the sector response for 2022 floods and conflict-affected population. UNICEF has generated good data and evidence-base on sanitation and drinking water situation in the country and used these to enable the GoS to develop several plans, policies and road maps, including the important National Water Supply. At the same time, close to 1,500 communities have been certified OD-free up to the end of 2021 and another 510 added to this category at the end of 2022, contributing to more children and their families (are) living in an open-defecation-free environment. In the area of public finance for children (PF4C), UNICEF supported a study on Child Focused Expenditure Review, 2016-2022 at national level and state level for the six states of Blue Nile, Gedaref, Kassala, Khartoum, North Darfur and North Kordofan. Building on this review, UNICEF supported the design of a capacity-building plan for state- and locality-level finance and sectoral planning officers, which included the development of a state level curriculum on sectoral planning, budget formulation, implementation, monitoring and accounting for health and nutrition, education, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and social protection. Despite the challenging operational environment in 2022, UNICEFs contribution to advancing gains in the WASH sector was significant. UNICEF-supported initiatives led to the issuing of open defecation free (ODF) certification for 510 communities (91 per cent of all WASH sector achievement and 85 per cent of the UNICEF target), with around 523,000 people realizing their basic right to sanitation (86 per cent of the sector achievement) and more than 152,000 people moving up the sanitation ladder. By investing in building the capacity of partners in community-led total sanitation (CLTS) and increasing the drive for the sanitation marketing approach, Sudanese children and their families eliminated open defecation and started using some form of sanitation, reducing the risk of soil, food and groundwater contamination, and leading to a cleaner environment. UNICEF has developed a scale-up plan for Mother and Child Cash Transfers (MCCT), stepping up efforts to build strategic alliances with key donors and partners funding social protection programmes in Sudan. The aim of the programme is to support the first thousand days of a child's life and promote women's health through the provision of care services for pregnant and lactating women and capacity building for midwives in rural and urban areas. The programme builds on UNICEF's integrated approach by promoting safe health and nutrition practices among beneficiaries and extending WASH services to targeted communities. UNICEF strengthened its internal capacity in cash programming by establishing a Cash Implementation Unit. In addition, UNICEF introduced the global cash transfer management information system, HOPE, which enabled direct support to frontline workers providing critical services, including teachers, health and social workers. More than 50,500 pregnant and lactating women and their 252,600 household members were successfully reached by 2022. UNICEF has also mobilised resources to reach an additional target of 30,000 pregnant and lactating women, for a total of 180,000 people.
